title: Social Security Protection Requirements for Crew on Singapore-based and Foreign-based Maritime Vessels
what_it_is: Social Security Protection Requirements for Crew on Singapore-based and Foreign-based Maritime Vessels

sections.label: Singapore seafarer protection measures
sections.summary: Singapore ratified the Maritime Labour Convention in 2011 and provides medical, injury, invalidity and CPF benefits for seafarers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Singapore is committed to protecting the well-being of seafarers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: In 2011, Singapore was the first country in Asia to ratify the Maritime Labour Convention (MLC), which is a comprehensive global labour instrument adopted by the International Labour Organization to provide for the rights and protection of seafarers working onboard vessels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Our legislation provides for medical care, employment injury and invalidity benefits for all seafarers, Singaporeans or otherwise, employed on Singapore-flagged vessels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: In addition, Singaporean seafarers who enter into employment in Singapore and their employers are generally required to make CPF contributions for the seafarers' retirement needs, regardless of whether they are working on Singapore or foreign-flagged vessels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore has not come across any cases of Singaporean seafarers who have been denied the requisite social security benefits.
